questions.stem: This chest overlay maps the four cardiac auscultation areas (A-P-T and the apex). The systolic ejection murmur of aortic stenosis is heard best at area 'A'; where does this murmur characteristically radiate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To the interscapular region of the back

choices.label: B
choices.text: To the left lower sternal border

explanation.summary: The aortic area sits at the right second intercostal space. Aortic stenosis produces a crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur that radiates upward along the direction of turbulent flow into the carotid arteries (radiation to the axilla instead suggests mitral regurgitation).
explanation.whyCorrect: The aortic area sits at the right second intercostal space. Aortic stenosis produces a crescendo-decrescendo systolic ejection murmur that radiates upward along the direction of turbulent flow into the carotid arteries (radiation to the axilla instead suggests mitral regurgitation).

questions.stem: In this clinical photograph a pulse oximeter on the toe reads 80% while one on the finger reads 95%. This finding of lower saturation in the lower body than the upper body is termed what?

explanation.summary: Differential cyanosis (pink upper body, cyanotic lower body) occurs when deoxygenated blood shunts right-to-left through a patent ductus arteriosus into the descending aorta distal to the arch vessels, as in a PDA with pulmonary hypertension/Eisenmenger physiology or a coarctation with PDA.

questions.stem: This echocardiogram (right panel with color Doppler) demonstrates abnormal flow through a connection between the main pulmonary artery and the descending aorta. In an uncomplicated case, in which direction does blood flow through this connection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No net flow because aortic and pulmonary pressures are equal

choices.label: B
choices.text: From the left atrium into the right atrium

choices.label: C
choices.text: From the pulmonary artery into the aorta (right-to-left)

choices.label: D
choices.text: From the pulmonary artery to the aorta only during diastole

choices.label: E
choices.text: From the aorta into the pulmonary artery (left-to-right)

explanation.summary: Aortic pressure exceeds pulmonary artery pressure throughout the cardiac cycle, so a patent ductus arteriosus carries a continuous left-to-right (aorta-to-pulmonary-artery) shunt. Color Doppler shows this as turbulent flow entering the pulmonary artery near the descending aorta.
explanation.whyCorrect: Aortic pressure exceeds pulmonary artery pressure throughout the cardiac cycle, so a patent ductus arteriosus carries a continuous left-to-right (aorta-to-pulmonary-artery) shunt. Color Doppler shows this as turbulent flow entering the pulmonary artery near the descending aorta.

questions.stem: This anterior cutaway shows an opening in the wall between the two upper chambers with blood crossing through it. Under normal chamber pressures, in which direction does blood shunt across this defect and what is the immediate hemodynamic result?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Left-to-right shunt that lowers left atrial pressure

choices.label: D
choices.text: Left-to-right shunt causing right heart volume overload

choices.label: E
choices.text: Bidirectional shunt with no net flow

explanation.summary: Because left atrial pressure normally exceeds right atrial pressure, an atrial septal defect produces an acyanotic left-to-right shunt. The extra volume returning to the right heart and lungs causes right atrial/ventricular volume overload and pulmonary overcirculation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because left atrial pressure normally exceeds right atrial pressure, an atrial septal defect produces an acyanotic left-to-right shunt. The extra volume returning to the right heart and lungs causes right atrial/ventricular volume overload and pulmonary overcirculation.

questions.stem: This view of the atrial septum marks several possible locations for an interatrial communication. A defect at the most ventral/inferior location adjacent to the AV valves (the primum type) is characteristically associated with which other anomaly?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A cleft anterior mitral valve leaflet

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ebstein anomaly of the tricuspid valve

explanation.summary: Ostium primum ASDs arise from failure of endocardial cushion fusion, so they occur low in the septum near the AV valves and are frequently accompanied by a cleft mitral valve and AV canal defects, classically in trisomy 21. (Sinus venosus defects, by contrast, associate with anomalous pulmonary venous drainage.)
explanation.whyCorrect: Ostium primum ASDs arise from failure of endocardial cushion fusion, so they occur low in the septum near the AV valves and are frequently accompanied by a cleft mitral valve and AV canal defects, classically in trisomy 21. questions.stem: This cutaway shows a communication in the wall separating the two pumping chambers, with a shunt arrow crossing from one to the other. What auscultatory finding does this lesion classically produce?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A systolic ejection murmur that increases with inspiration

choices.label: C
choices.text: A mid-diastolic rumble at the apex

choices.label: E
choices.text: A holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border

explanation.summary: A ventricular septal defect drives a left-to-right shunt throughout systole because left ventricular pressure exceeds right ventricular pressure for the entire ejection period, producing a harsh holosystolic murmur best heard at the left lower sternal border. Interestingly, smaller VSDs are often louder.
explanation.whyCorrect: A ventricular septal defect drives a left-to-right shunt throughout systole because left ventricular pressure exceeds right ventricular pressure for the entire ejection period, producing a harsh holosystolic murmur best heard at the left lower sternal border. Interestingly, smaller VSDs are often louder.

questions.stem: This diagram shows persistent postnatal patency of the vessel connecting the aorta and pulmonary artery, with resulting increased pulmonary flow and an enlarged left ventricle. What is the characteristic auscultatory finding of this lesion?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A systolic ejection click radiating to the carotids

choices.label: C
choices.text: An opening snap followed by a diastolic rumble

choices.label: D
choices.text: A holosystolic murmur at the lower sternal border

explanation.summary: Because aortic pressure exceeds pulmonary pressure in both systole and diastole, a patent ductus arteriosus shunts blood left-to-right throughout the cardiac cycle, producing a continuous 'machinery' murmur. Chronic left-heart volume overload causes left ventricular/atrial enlargement.
explanation.whyCorrect: Because aortic pressure exceeds pulmonary pressure in both systole and diastole, a patent ductus arteriosus shunts blood left-to-right throughout the cardiac cycle, producing a continuous 'machinery' murmur. Chronic left-heart volume overload causes left ventricular/atrial enlargement.

questions.stem: This five-stage sequence traces the formation and apposition of two membranous partitions that divide the primitive common atrium. What normally happens to these structures at birth?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The septum primum perforates to create a new ostium secundum after birth

choices.label: B
choices.text: The septum secundum degenerates, leaving the foramen ovale permanently open

choices.label: C
choices.text: The endocardial cushions fuse to form the interventricular septum

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ostium primum enlarges to become the coronary sinus

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rising left atrial pressure presses the septum primum against the septum secundum

explanation.summary: During fetal life blood shunts right-to-left through the foramen ovale (between the ostium secundum and the septum secundum). After birth, increased pulmonary venous return raises left atrial pressure, pushing the flap-like septum primum against the septum secundum and functionally closing the foramen ovale; failure to seal leaves a patent foramen ovale.
explanation.whyCorrect: During fetal life blood shunts right-to-left through the foramen ovale (between the ostium secundum and the septum secundum). After birth, increased pulmonary venous return raises left atrial pressure, pushing the flap-like septum primum against the septum secundum and functionally closing the foramen ovale; failure to seal leaves a patent foramen ovale.

questions.stem: This diagram contrasts the normal respiratory variation in the second heart sound with a pattern that stays widely split and unchanged between inspiration and expiration. The lower ('fixed, wide') pattern is the classic auscultatory sign of which lesion?

explanation.summary: In an ASD the left-to-right shunt equalizes right and left atrial filling across the respiratory cycle, so right ventricular ejection (and thus P2 timing relative to A2) no longer varies with inspiration. This produces a fixed, widely split S2.
explanation.whyCorrect: In an ASD the left-to-right shunt equalizes right and left atrial filling across the respiratory cycle, so right ventricular ejection (and thus P2 timing relative to A2) no longer varies with inspiration. This produces a fixed, widely split S2.

questions.stem: This schematic shows fusion of the endocardial cushions and the septa that partition the atrioventricular canal and the ventricles. Failure of the membranous portion forming at the top of the ventricular septum to close results in which defect?

explanation.summary: The interventricular septum closes last at its membranous portion, where the endocardial cushions, muscular septum, and conotruncal ridges meet. Failure of these to fuse leaves a membranous VSD, the most common type of ventricular septal defect.
explanation.whyCorrect: The interventricular septum closes last at its membranous portion, where the endocardial cushions, muscular septum, and conotruncal ridges meet. Failure of these to fuse leaves a membranous VSD, the most common type of ventricular septal defect.

questions.stem: These paired diagrams give oxygen-saturation values throughout the heart in a normal patient and in one with the labeled defect; note the right ventricle rises from 75% to 83%. This oxygen 'step-up' in the right ventricle is direct evidence of what?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A right-to-left shunt at the ventricular level

choices.label: C
choices.text: A left-to-right shunt at the atrial level

choices.label: E
choices.text: A left-to-right shunt at the ventricular level

explanation.summary: Fully saturated left ventricular blood crossing a VSD mixes into the deoxygenated right ventricular blood, raising RV saturation above the expected ~75%. A saturation step-up localizes the shunt to the chamber where it first appears (here the right ventricle), confirming a left-to-right VSD.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fully saturated left ventricular blood crossing a VSD mixes into the deoxygenated right ventricular blood, raising RV saturation above the expected ~75%. A saturation step-up localizes the shunt to the chamber where it first appears (here the right ventricle), confirming a left-to-right VSD.

questions.stem: This diagram traces blood flow through the fetal heart and its three shunts. What is the primary functional purpose of the shunt (labeled at the great vessels) that connects the pulmonary artery to the aorta?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To shunt blood from the left atrium into the right atrium

choices.label: B
choices.text: To bypass the fetal liver with placental blood

choices.label: C
choices.text: To deliver oxygenated blood to the fetal lungs for gas exchange

choices.label: D
choices.text: To divert blood away from the non-functioning fetal lungs

choices.label: E
choices.text: To equalize pressure between the two ventricles

explanation.summary: The ductus arteriosus shunts blood from the pulmonary artery to the aorta, bypassing the high-resistance, fluid-filled fetal lungs. (The foramen ovale bypasses the lungs at the atrial level, and the ductus venosus bypasses the liver.) It normally closes after birth as oxygen tension rises and prostaglandins fall.
explanation.whyCorrect: The ductus arteriosus shunts blood from the pulmonary artery to the aorta, bypassing the high-resistance, fluid-filled fetal lungs. (The foramen ovale bypasses the lungs at the atrial level, and the ductus venosus bypasses the liver.) It normally closes after birth as oxygen tension rises and prostaglandins fall.
